speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old female. The patient presents with a 5-day history of severe abdominal pain and cramping, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. She reports pain with urination and also experienced burning pain during sexual intercourse 3 days ago. She mentions being sexually active with one male partner, using condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID) with concurrent pyelonephritis.

Your history of sexual activity, dysuria, and recent sexual pain is highly suggestive of a pelvic infection, likely involving the upper genital tract, which can also refer pain to the abdomen. Given your severe symptoms and elevated white blood cell count, I will immediately start empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics covering typical sexually transmitted pathogens and uropathogens. Do you have any known allergies to penicillin or cephalosporins?
